verdict.reasoning: The doctor confirms, “it says you're feeling short of breath. Is that correct?” and the patient responds, “Yeah,” indicating she reports shortness of breath.

Patient states, “over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath” and confirms this was “while you're sitting watching tv,” indicating onset about one hour ago at rest watching TV.
Patient says, “So I started with a cough yesterday,” and when asked, “Have you brought anything up?” she replies, “No, I haven't. No,” supporting non‑productive cough since yesterday.

Patient reports, “I had a C section a few weeks ago… Yeah. Four weeks.” and when asked about the baby: “And how is baby doing?” she replies, “Yep, he's good,” indicating four weeks postpartum after C‑section and baby is well.
When asked, “How about when you take a very deep breath in?” patient answers, “I mean, yeah, my chest feels sore,” indicating soreness with deep inspiration.
In the same response, patient adds, “but so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender,” indicating the C‑section scar is tender.

Patient states, “I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart is really going,” and the clinician reflects, “you're feeling your heart more than normal?” with patient replying “Yeah,” indicating stress/anxiety about a rapid heartbeat.
When asked, “have you noticed anything like this before?” regarding shortness of breath, patient responds, “No,” indicating no prior episodes.

The transcript notes a cough and that she had coughs and colds “a good few months ago,” but there is no discussion of fever or an explicit statement that there is no recent illness other than the cough.
Clinician asks, “And the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest?” and patient answers, “No,” supporting no chest pain.
Patient states, “I had a C section a few weeks ago… Yeah. Four weeks,” supporting four weeks status post cesarean section.
Patient says of codeine, “Yeah, I've been taking that fairly regularly, but probably haven't taken it for a week,” indicating regular use with last use about a week ago.
When asked about allergies, patient says, “I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though.” When asked, “And what happens when you take ibuprofen?” she replies, “I don't know,” leaving the reaction unspecified.

Patient confirms, “Yes, I am” when asked if she is with baby, and later, “Is anyone else with you at home?” she answers, “No, my partner's at work,” indicating baby present, partner at work, no one else at home.
After timed counting, the clinician asks, “How many did you count?” and patient says, “I counted 30,” indicating 30 heartbeats in the counting interval.
Patient repeatedly acknowledges current shortness of breath: initial confirmation “Yeah” to “you're feeling short of breath,” and description of onset over the last hour.
Patient reports, “So I started with a cough yesterday,” directly supporting cough since yesterday.
As in hpi-009, patient responds “No” when asked if the shortness of breath causes any chest pain, supporting no chest pain.
When asked about deep breath, patient says, “yeah, my chest feels sore, but so does my C section scar,” indicating deep breathing is associated with chest/chest wall tenderness.
Patient states, “but so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender,” confirming tenderness of the cesarean scar by her report.
Patient confirms baby is with her (“Yes, I am” to being with baby) and “Yep, he's good,” indicating baby is present and well.

Clinician explicitly expresses concern: “given that you've had a C section… some people can suffer with clots, and those can either be found in the legs or… your chest. So in your lungs,” and advises hospital evaluation, matching concern for postpartum VTE/PE.
While a cough since yesterday is documented, there is no explicit assessment in the transcript labeling it as viral URI or benign; that interpretation is not stated.

Postoperative status is clear from “I had a C section… four weeks,” and patient reports “my chest feels sore, but so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender,” supporting chest wall/pleuritic-type discomfort and scar tenderness post‑C‑section.
Ibuprofen allergy and codeine use are noted, but there is no discussion of evaluating analgesia requirements in the emergency department.

Clinician says, “it might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further,” and later explains concern about clots in legs or lungs, matching urgent ED evaluation for PE or other causes of SOB today.

Clinician offers options: “I can call an ambulance or you can take yourself to the hospital with baby. Which one would you prefer?” Patient replies, “I'll go. I'll take myself,” and doctor advises, “go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time.”
The clinician only states, “if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them for the time being.” There is no mention of NSAIDs or linking this to her ibuprofen allergy.
